title: Why is the world watching the Taiwan Strait?

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why is the world watching the Taiwan Strait?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About a hundred and thirty kilometres of water between China and Taiwan, and one of the busiest sea lanes on Earth.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where exactly is it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Between China's Fujian coast and the island of Taiwan. It links the East and South China Seas.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: From space, you can see both shores at once.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who ruled Taiwan first?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Its own Austronesian peoples. Then, in 1624, the Dutch built Fort Zeelandia and ran a trading colony.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1661, the Ming loyalist Koxinga besieged it. Early in 1662, the Dutch surrendered.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And then China took it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The Qing dynasty did, in 1683. After losing a war in 1895, it handed Taiwan to Japan, which ruled until 1945.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So how did Taiwan split from China?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Civil war. In 1949, the Communists won the mainland, and Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists retreated to Taiwan.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Both governments claimed to be the real China.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did America get involved?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1950, when the Korean War began, Truman sent the Seventh Fleet into the strait.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1958, China shelled Kinmen, a Taiwanese island just off the mainland, for weeks. American ships and jets backed Taiwan.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does the whole world care?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 2022, nearly half the world's container ships sailed through it. And Taiwan makes about ninety percent of the most advanced chips.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And today?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: China says Taiwan is part of its territory and has not ruled out force. Its navy often holds drills around the island.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: the Bosphorus. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
